matches.description: Watch River Plate vs Atletico Tucuman highlights and goals from Argentine Primera División on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 4, 2026. The Liga Profesional Argentina took center stage on May 4, 2026 , as two of the nation's most competitive sides met in a high-stakes clash filled with tactical intrigue. Fans expected a battle of nerves, and the match delivered an intense spectacle where defensive discipline and a single moment of clinical finishing would define the afternoon. Early Breakthrough Sets the Tone The match burst into life early on when the visitors seized the initiative and capitalized on a defensive lapse. In the 19th minute, a well-orchestrated move saw Maximiliano Villa find space to deliver a precise ball into the path of Renzo Tesuri . Showing great composure under pressure, Tesuri found the back of the net to give Atletico Tucuman an early advantage, sending the traveling support into raptures and forcing River Plate to rethink their strategy for the remainder of the first half . As the opening period progressed, the tempo remained high but clear-cut chance creation became harder to come by. River Plate attempted to dictate the play through possession, but the defensive discipline of the opposition proved difficult to break down. The physical nature of the contest became evident just before the interval when Leonel Vega received a yellow card in the 42nd minute for a mistimed challenge, reflecting the growing tension on the pitch as the teams headed into the locker rooms. River Plate’s Tactical Reset in the Second Half Seeking a way back into the game, River Plate made a significant triple substitution at the start of the second half . Kendry Paez , Lautaro Pereyra , and Maximiliano Salas were introduced to provide fresh impetus in the final third, replacing Ian Subiabre , Maximiliano Meza , and Agustin Ruberto . The home side immediately showed more urgency, though the flow of the sports spectacle remained stop-start due to frequent fouls. Lautaro Godoy was cautioned early in the period, and shortly after, River turned to the bench again, bringing on the creative Juan Quintero in place of Tomas Galvan to try and unlock the stubborn Atletico Tucuman backline. Despite the mounting pressure and a series of tactical shifts, the visitors stood their ground with remarkable resilience. Gaston Suso was replaced by Luciano Vallejo to maintain defensive stability, while the goal hero Renzo Tesuri made way for Gabriel Compagnucci as the visitors looked to shore up their lead for the final ten minutes. The defensive block remained compact, forcing the hosts into wide areas and speculative crosses that were dealt with effectively. Late Drama and Defensive Resilience The final minutes were frantic as River Plate threw everything forward in search of an equalizer. Kendry Paez picked up a yellow card in the 88th minute as frustration mounted for the hosts, who struggled to find a decisive opening. Atletico Tucuman managed the closing stages with professional efficiency, utilizing a flurry of late substitutions, including the entry of Manuel Brondo and Kevin Ortiz , to disrupt the rhythm of the game. With seven minutes of stoppage time added, the tension reached a boiling point. River Plate made one final change, introducing Joaquin Freitas for Fabricio Bustos , but they could not find the breakthrough they desperately needed. When the referee finally blew the whistle at the 90+7' mark, it confirmed a hard-earned victory for the away side, leaving the home fans to reflect on a frustrating afternoon of missed opportunities in this gripping football encounter.
